Fuel Quality Control Checklist

PRE-FUELING CHECKS:

☐ Fuel type confirmed with flight crew ☐ Quantity required confirmed

☐ Water drain checks performed (minimum 3 sumps) ☐ Filter/separator condition checked

☐ Sample taken and clear (no water, sediment) ☐ Fuel color/odor normal

☐ Bonding cable connected before fueling ☐ Vehicle grounding checked

☐ Fire extinguisher present and sealed ☐ No smoking signs posted

☐ Emergency shutoff location identified ☐ Communication with cockpit established

DURING FUELING:

☐ Bonding cable remains connected ☐ Flow rate monitored

☐ Personnel remain with vehicle ☐ Nozzle properly inserted

☐ Nozzle grounded to aircraft ☐ Pressure monitored

☐ Vehicle position monitored ☐ No leaks observed

☐ Quantity monitored (overfill prevention) ☐ Communication maintained

POST-FUELING:

☐ Final quantity confirmed with flight crew ☐ Fuel receipt signed

☐ Bonding cable disconnected after fueling ☐ Caps and covers secured

☐ Final sample taken (if required) ☐ Hose drained and stowed

☐ Vehicle moved safely from aircraft ☐ Area checked for spills

☐ Documentation completed ☐ Any discrepancies reported

Emergency Response Procedures - Fuel Spill Scenario

IMMEDIATE ACTIONS:

1. STOP fueling immediately (emergency shutoff)

2. ISOLATE ignition sources (engine, APU, electrical)

3. EVACUATE area of unnecessary personnel

4. NOTIFY emergency services (airport fire department)

5. ASSESS spill size and direction

6. CONTAIN spill using available materials

7. REPORT to supervisor and operations

SPILL CLASSIFICATION:

☐ MINOR (< 5 liters) - Handle locally with spill kit

☐ MODERATE (5-200 liters) - Airport fire department response

☐ MAJOR (>200 liters) - Full emergency response, possible runway closure
